labels.value: The string datatype represents character strings in XML. The value space of string is the set of finite-length sequences of characters.
The boolean datatype represents the values of two-valued logic: true or false. Valid values are: true, false, 1 (for true), 0 (for false).
The decimal datatype represents arbitrary precision decimal numbers. The value space of decimal is the set of numbers that can be represented by decimal numerals.
The float datatype represents IEEE single-precision 32-bit floating point numbers.
The double datatype represents IEEE double-precision 64-bit floating point numbers.

The duration datatype represents a duration of time. The pattern for duration is PnYnMnDTnHnMnS, where nY represents the number of years, nM the number of months, nD the number of days, T is the date/time separator, nH the number of hours, nM the number of minutes and nS the number of seconds.

The dateTime datatype represents a specific instant of time. The pattern for dateTime is CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss where CC represents the century, YY the year, MM the month and DD the day. The letter T is the date/time separator and hh, mm, ss represent hour, minute and second respectively.
The time datatype represents an instant of time that recurs every day. The pattern for time is hh:mm:ss.sss with optional following time zone indicator.
The date datatype represents a calendar date. The pattern for date is CCYY-MM-DD with optional time zone indicator.
The gYearMonth datatype represents a specific month in a specific year. The pattern for gYearMonth is CCYY-MM with optional time zone indicator.
The gYear datatype represents a specific Gregorian calendar year. The pattern for gYear is CCYY with optional time zone indicator.
The gMonthDay datatype represents a specific day that recurs every year. The pattern for gMonthDay is --MM-DD with optional time zone indicator.
The gDay datatype represents a day that recurs every month. The pattern for gDay is ---DD with optional time zone indicator.
The gMonth datatype represents a month that recurs every year. The pattern for gMonth is --MM with optional time zone indicator.
The hexBinary datatype represents arbitrary hex-encoded binary data.
The base64Binary datatype represents Base64-encoded arbitrary binary data.
The anyURI datatype represents a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) reference.
The QName datatype represents XML qualified names. A QName consists of a namespace name and a local part.
The NOTATION datatype represents a reference to a notation declared in the schema.

The normalizedString datatype represents white space normalized strings. The value space of normalizedString is the set of strings that do not contain the carriage return, line feed nor tab characters.

The token datatype represents tokenized strings. The value space of token is the set of strings that do not contain the carriage return, line feed, nor tab characters, that have no leading or trailing spaces, and that have no internal sequences of two or more spaces.
The language datatype represents natural language identifiers as defined by RFC 3066.
The NMTOKEN datatype represents a single token, as used in XML. NMTOKEN values may consist of letters, digits, periods, hyphens, underscores, and colons.
The Name datatype represents XML Names. Name values must start with a letter, underscore, or colon and may contain letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, colons, and periods.
The NCName datatype represents XML non-colonized Names. NCName values may not contain colons.
The ID datatype represents the ID attribute type from XML 1.0. ID values must uniquely identify elements in an XML document.
The IDREF datatype represents a reference to an element that has an ID attribute.
The ENTITY datatype represents a reference to an unparsed entity.
The integer datatype represents a sequence of decimal digits with an optional leading sign (+ or -). The value space of integer is the infinite set {...,-2,-1,0,1,2,...}.
The nonPositiveInteger datatype represents the infinite set of integers less than or equal to zero.
The negativeInteger datatype represents the infinite set of integers less than zero.
The long datatype represents a 64-bit signed integer with values from -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807.
The int datatype represents a 32-bit signed integer with values from -2147483648 to 2147483647.
The short datatype represents a 16-bit signed integer with values from -32768 to 32767.
The byte datatype represents an 8-bit signed integer with values from -128 to 127.
The nonNegativeInteger datatype represents the infinite set of integers greater than or equal to zero.
The unsignedLong datatype represents a 64-bit unsigned integer with values from 0 to 18446744073709551615.
The unsignedInt datatype represents a 32-bit unsigned integer with values from 0 to 4294967295.
The unsignedShort datatype represents a 16-bit unsigned integer with values from 0 to 65535.
The unsignedByte datatype represents an 8-bit unsigned integer with values from 0 to 255.
The positiveInteger datatype represents the infinite set of integers greater than zero.

The period dimension takes a value that is a time interval, which may be zero-length (i.e. an instant). This type defines a standard period string representation which can be used to express such values.The period string representation is obtained as follows: If the value is a non-zero length interval, then the representation is a pair of ISO 8601 date-time values, separated by the / character; Otherwise, the value is a single ISO 8601 date-time value. The date-time values used in this representation MUST be valid according to the xs:dateTime datatype and MUST be in the canonical lexical representation. The error code oimce:invalidPeriodRepresentation MUST be raised for values that are required to be a period string representation and which do not conform to the above format. It should be noted that unlike the xbrli:dateUnion type used in xBRL-XML, the xs:dateTime datatype used here does not allow the time component to be omitted.
The start and end dates of a period defined as a single type.

The unit dimension defines units in terms of the combination of QNames by defining an unordered collection of numerators and an unordered collection of denominators. This type defines a standardised unit string representation, allowing units to be captured using a unique string value. This has the property that, provided that a consistent set of namespace prefixes are used, a given unit will have a single representation meaning that equivalence of units can be determined by string comparison. The unit string representation is obtained as follows: If {denominators} is not present, the QNames representing the {numerators} are combined in lexicographic order, separated by the * character. Otherwise, lists of {numerators} and {denominators} are created by combining QNames in lexicographic order and separating with the * character, as above. If a list contains more than one item, the list is enclosed in parentheses. The final string is then obtained by concatenating the list of numerators, the / character, and the list of denominators. Whitespace is not permitted anywhere in the string representation, and the use of QNames ensures that a 1:1 mapping between prefixes and namespaces is available thus ensuring that equivalent units appearing within the same document are represented with the same string. Lexicographic order means ordered based on comparison of Unicode code point values of each character. If any QNames in the unit string representation use a prefix that is not defined in the prefix map then oimce:unboundPrefix MUST be raised.
The aggregation data type is used to uniquely identify the method of aggregation used to generate a single value from a population.

The monetary type serves as the data type for those financial concepts in a taxonomy which denote units in a currency. Instance items with this type must have a unit of measure from the ISO 4217 namespace of currencies.
This data type serves as the type for dimensionless numbers such as percentage change, growth rates, and other ratios where the numerator and denominator have the same units.
The enumeration type defines an XBRL item type which takes an XML Name in the format 'namespace-uri#localname' as a value.

escaped specializes string. There is no constraint on whether the resulting unescaped content is well-formed or not; this base type exists so that processors know what to do with the content. It is a suitable base type for a data type whose unescaped content must be valid HTML 4.0 (which is not XML).
xmlNodes specializes escaped. The unescaped content MUST be a sequence of XML text and well-formed XML nodes. This content constraint cannot be captured by a finite length regular expression.
xml specializes xmlNodes. The unescaped content MUST be well-formed XML. This is a suitable base type for elements whose content must conform to a specific XML Schema or DTD.
textBlock specializes xmlNodes. The unescaped content MUST have mixed content containing a simple string, or a fragment of XHTML or a mixture of both.

The percent item type is used to indicate that the value of the element is intended to be presented as a percentage. This does not contravene Specification section 4.8.2, which requires that percentages not be multiplied by 100.
The per share item type indicates a monetary amount divided by a number of shares. The per share item type has a Decimal base.
The area item type is used to indicate that an element represents an area.
The Volume item type is used to indicate that an element represents a volume and can be used to express the volume of any substance, whether solid, liquid, or gas.
The mass item type represents the mass of an object which can be measured.
The weight item type represents the weight of an object which can be measured.
The energy item type represents a unit of energy.
Measures a rate of energy use or energy production and is equivalent to the use or production of energy during a period of time. I.e. a watt is the equal to one joule of energy per second.
The length item type is a measure of distance.
The memory item type is a measure of memory typically used in the IT industry.

The NoDecimalsMonetary is a restriction on the xbrlr:monetary in that it does not allow cents on the monetary value. Facts using this type MUST have an (inferred) decimals attribute value that is less than or equal to zero, or 'INF'.
The nonNegativeMonetary is a restriction on the xbrlr:monetary in that it does not allow negative values on the monetary value.

The nonNegativeNoDecimalsMonetary is a restriction on the xbrlr:monetary in that it does not allow cents or negative values on the monetary value. Facts using this type MUST have an (inferred) decimals attribute value that is less than or equal to zero, or 'INF'.
The insolation item type is used to represent a measure of energy per area over a period of time.
The temperature item type is used to represent a measure of temperature either in absolute terms or as a difference between two temperatures.

The pressure item type is used to represent a measure of the force applied perpendicular to the surface of an object per unit area over which that force is distributed. Units include Pascal, PSI and Bar.
The frequency item type is used to represent a measure of the number of occurrences of a repeating event per unit time.
The irradiance item type is used to represent a measure irradiance (power per unit area)
The speed item type is used to represent a measure of speed (distance traveled by an object per unit time). Units include knots, mach, and metres per second.
The angle item type is used to represent the measurement of an angle. Units include radians, degrees and gradians.
The voltage item type is used to represent a measure of voltage (the difference in electric potential energy between two points per unit electric charge).
The electric current item type is used to represent a measure of electric current (the flow of electric charge over a circuit).
The force item type is used to represent a measure of a physical force. Units include newtons.
The electric charge item is used to represent a measure of electric charge (the physical property of matter that causes it to experience a force when placed in an electromagnetic field)

The purpose of the guidance type is to identify 'guidance items' which provide general guidance for users of a taxonomy, particularly preparers of XBRL reports. Guidance is defined as a property value of the xbrl:abstractDataType property defined ona  a heading object. This property allows guidance to be positioned in appropriate locations in the parent-child relationship network, and is intended to help users who view the taxonomy through displays based on the parent-child relationship network. Guidance items provide general guidance which is not limited to the application of a specific tag to an individual item of data. This remains as a datatype but can only be used as a property value, to support backward compatability to XBRL 2.1 taxonomies.
This data type allows the reporting of a list of xsd:gYear values as a single value
The flow item type is used to represent a measure of volumetric flow rate.
The mass flow item type is used to represent a measure of mass flow rate.
The monetary per length item type is used to represent a measure of price or cost per unit length
The monetary per area item type is used to represent a measure of price or cost per unit area
The monetary per volume item type is used to represent a measure of price or cost per unit volume
The monetary per duration item type is used to represent a measure of price or cost per unit duration
The monetary per energy item type is used to represent a measure of price or cost per unit energy
The monetary per mass item type is used to represent a measure of price or cost per unit mass
A subtype of xs:dateTime that requires a time component (as xs:dateTime does).

An ISO 8601 truncated date/time value that may represent a year (YYYY), year-month (YYYY-MM), full date (YYYY-MM-DD), or date with hours, minutes or seconds. Used where the precision of a date or time value is not known in advance.
The greenhouse gas emissions item type is used in preference to mass to measure Global Warming Potential, which is often expressed in terms of tonnes of CO2 equivalent.
The energy per monetary item type is used to represent a measure of energy per monetary unit.
The emissions per monetary item type is used to represent a measure of GHG emissions per monetary unit.
The volume per monetary item type is used to represent a measure of volume per monetary unit.

At times an entity may restate certain account balances for financial reporting purposes. This may only occur according to specific reporting rules. For example, an entity may restate an equity account balance, say 'Reserves', due to an accounting change or fundamental error under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). A separate label role is provided for such reporting of restated amounts, should they occur. The restated amount within a financial statement might provide a label such as 'Reserves, Restated Balance' to which this label role would be assigned to identify this type of label. Taxonomy creators would use this label role and provide a label which could be used on concepts that could be restated. Typically, these would be used on equity accounts.
Label for a unit, when the unit is represented by a symbol.

Represents the concept core dimension in a taxonomy.  The concept dimension is used to identify concepts that have  measurable facts (for example, a numeric or textual fact). Concepts have data types, period types and may have properties and labels.

Represents the unit core dimension in a taxonomy. Only unit objects can be added to the unit dimension. Each unit object defines the unit of measure associated with numeric facts, for example 'USD' or 'ug/m3'. Units may be simple or composed with numerators and denominators.
The period core dimension identifies the reporting period associated with a fact. Period values may be instants, durations, or open intervals, depending on the taxonomy.

The entity core dimension identifies the reporting entity or subject of the fact. Entity identifiers used on this dimension may be expressed as LEIs, names or other identifiers as defined by the taxonomy.
A domain used to express trait values or annotations that can be applied to objects. Trait domains are typically used to model property-like annotations in the taxonomy.
A concept domain groups concept members that can be referenced by cubes and dimensions. It is the domain used when a cube restricts the concept dimension to a subset of concepts.
A unit domain groups unit definitions for use by concepts and facts. It allows taxonomies to declare a set of preferred or allowed units.
A semantic link is a relationship type used to express semantic associations between objects, for example to indicate equivalence, suggested mappings or explanatory links.
A weight link property is used on certain relationship types (for example summation-concept) to indicate the multiplier applied to the source when computing aggregates.

A reconciliation link property is a boolean value used on a summation-concept relationship types to indicate that the source and target xbrla:balance can be the same and have a -1 weight or be different and have a +1 weight.
The preferredLabel link property indicates which label role should be used as the preferred human-readable label for presentation.
Report attributes are properties attached to concepts objects to indicate how a concept in a taxonomy maps to standard report attributes such as reporting period end, or report type.
A traitLinkType is a custom link property used to express typed property relationships between objects and trait domains.
The parent-child relationship type is used to build hierarchical structures (trees) between model objects such as concepts, members, and domains.
The class-subclass relationship type expresses a subclassing relationship between concepts indicating a tighter or more specific definition.
A propertyValue-object link expresses the assignment of a property value to a target model object, used to model custom properties in the taxonomy.
The concept-refDimension relationship links a concept to a dimension indicating that the value of the concept in a detailed cube may be the key of a dimension is a summarized cube.
Cube type representing a report or statement where period and entity core dimensions are expected.

Cube type used for negative assertions and exclusions in validation rules. Based on xbrl:reportCube, it specifies dimensional combinations that should NOT appear in a report or are prohibited in certain contexts. Negative cubes are commonly used in taxonomy validation to define forbidden fact patterns or to express constraints on what dimensional combinations are invalid.
Core dimension used to indicate the language of a fact where applicable.
Relationship type that indicates the target contributes to the source as part of a summation (aggregation) with an associated weight.
The name this relationship type carried in the published PWD, accepted as an alias of xbrl:summation-concept until the published documents are updated.
Relationship type used to indicate a general-to-special relationship between concepts (a refinement or more specific version).
Relationship type that links a concept to a dimension when the concept represents an aggregation over that dimension (aggregation specified on the relationship).
Relationship type indicating a unit applies to a fact concept or group of concepts.
Relationship type used for mapping unit-fact constructs between concept objects when unit-specific facts are modelled.
Represents a fact or data point in an XBRL report. Facts contain one or more fact values along with their dimensional context (concept, period, entity, unit, and other dimensions).

The taxonomy model type defines the structure and metadata for an XBRL taxonomy. Taxonomies contain concepts, dimensions, cubes, relationships, networks, labels, references, and other objects that define the reporting framework. A taxonomy provides the semantic framework that defines what can be reported and how it should be structured.

The report model type represents an XBRL instance document or report containing actual fact data. Reports contain facts, footnotes, entities, and units that provide the actual reported information according to the rules defined in one or more taxonomies. Each report must specify a report date and typically references one or more taxonomies that define the valid reporting structures and concepts.
Standard fact map for mapping facts from OIM JSON format to the XBRL model format. This map handles the transformation of JSON-based XBRL data into the Open Information Model structure.

Standard fact map for mapping facts from traditional XBRL 2.1 XML format to the XBRL model format. This map handles the transformation of XML-based XBRL v2.1 instance documents into the Open Information Model structure.
Defines the association between a cube and a dimension, specifying which dimensions are used in a particular cube structure and any constraints on those dimensions.
Defines a type of cube structure that specifies core dimensions and constraints. Cube types provide templates for creating cubes with predefined dimensional structures.
Defines a data type that can be used for concept values, extending or restricting XML Schema data types with XBRL-specific semantics and validation rules.
Represents a domain member that can be used as a valid value on a dimension. Domains organize the members that categorize facts along a particular dimension.

Defines a mapping template for transforming facts from external formats (XBRL 2.1 XML, OIM JSON, CSV, etc.) into the XBRL model format. Fact maps specify how to extract dimensions, values, and metadata from source data.
Links a fact map to a specific data source, enabling the import of facts from external files or systems. Fact sources specify the location and format of external fact data.
Marks a taxonomy as final, preventing further imports or extensions. Final taxonomies are sealed and cannot be modified or extended by importing models.
Represents a footnote or explanatory note that provides additional context, explanations, or disclosures related to facts in the report.
Defines the content model for a group, specifying which objects or patterns can appear within the group structure.
Defines a reusable group of model objects that can be referenced by multiple networks or structures, promoting modularity and reuse in taxonomy design.
Represents a specific instantiation of a group with its hierarchical tree structure, including any local modifications or extensions to the base group definition.
Declares the import of another taxonomy, making its objects and definitions available for use. Imports support modular taxonomy development and selective object inclusion.
Provides human-readable text labels for model objects in different languages and label types (standard, terse, verbose, documentation, etc.).
Defines a type of label that can be associated with model objects, such as standard labels, terse labels, documentation, or custom label types for specific purposes.
Represents a member that can be used as a valid value for dimensions. Members provide the enumeration values for typed or explicit dimensions.
Defines constraints on XBRL models by specifying allowed object types, allowed properties, and required properties. Model types enable regulatory authorities to define specific report profiles.
Associates a property value with a model object, allowing the attachment of additional metadata and characteristics to concepts, dimensions, and other taxonomy elements.
Defines a type of property that can be attached to model objects, specifying the property's data type, allowed objects, and whether it is definitional.
Defines a type of reference that can link model objects to authoritative literature, standards, or documentation sources.
The root model object representing an entire XBRL taxonomy or report. Contains all objects, relationships, and metadata that comprise a complete XBRL model.

A built-in property type that specifies the default BCP 47 language for text-valued objects (such as footnotes and text-typed facts) within the model. When a text-valued object does not declare an explicit language, processors MAY use the value of this property on the enclosing XBRL model object as the inherited language. This property may only be applied to the xbrl:xbrlModelObject.
The HTML id attribute value of the span element whose inner text content contributes to the fact value.

Integers are 1-based and count element children only.

prefixedContent denotes values that rely for correct interpretation on namespace-prefix bindings in scope at the point of use. All item types that involve prefixed content should derive (directly or indirectly) from QName or prefixedContent Processors MUST raise an error if they encounter a fact with a type that is a subtype of prefixedContent that they do not recognise (unless that subtype is itself derived from a subtype that is recognised) as knowledge of the structure of the prefixed content is required to correctly preserve and present such content.

A temperature scale based on 0° for the freezing point of water and 100° for the boiling point of water at 1 atm pressure.

The kelvin is a unit of measure for temperature based upon an absolute scale. It is one of the seven base units in the International System of Units (SI) and is assigned the unit symbol K. The Kelvin scale is an absolute, thermodynamic temperature scale using as its null point absolute zero, the temperature at which all thermal motion ceases in the classical description of thermodynamics. The kelvin is defined as the fraction 1⁄273.16 of the thermodynamic temperature of the triple point of water (exactly 0.01 °C or 32.018 °F). In other words, it is defined such that the triple point of water is exactly 273.16 K.

Fahrenheit is a unit of measure for temperature defined by two fixed points: the temperature at which water freezes into ice is defined as 32 °F, and the boiling point of water is defined to be 212 °F, a 180 °F separation, as defined at sea level and standard atmospheric pressure.
The pascal is the SI derived unit of pressure used to quantify internal pressure, stress, Young's modulus and ultimate tensile strength. It is defined as one newton per square meter.

The bar is a metric unit of pressure, but is not approved as part of the International System of Units (SI). It is defined as exactly equal to 100000 Pa, which is slightly less than the current average atmospheric pressure on Earth at sea level.
The pound per square inch is a unit of pressure or of stress based on avoirdupois units. It is the pressure resulting from a force of one pound-force applied to an area of one square inch.
The standard atmosphere is a unit of pressure defined as 101325 Pa (1.01325 bar). It is sometimes used as a reference or standard pressure.

The newton is the International System of Units (SI) derived unit of force. One newton is the force needed to accelerate one kilogram of mass at the rate of one metre per second squared in direction of the applied force.

In electric power transmission and distribution, volt-ampere reactive (var) is a unit by which reactive power is expressed in an AC electric power system. Reactive power is the power that is wasted and not used to do work on the load.

A volt-ampere (VA) is the unit used for the apparent power in an electrical circuit, equal to the product of root-mean-square (RMS) voltage and RMS current. In direct current (DC) circuits, this product is equal to the real power (active power) in watts. Volt-amperes are useful only in the context of alternating current (AC) circuits.
An ampere hour or amp hour is a unit of electric charge, equal to the charge transferred by a steady current of one ampere flowing for one hour.
The coulomb is the International System of Units (SI) unit of electric charge. It is the charge transported by a constant current of one ampere in one second.
The degree is a measurement of a plane angle, defined so that a full rotation is 360 degrees. In XBRL the degree is reported in a decimal format.
The radian is the standard unit of angular measure. The radian is an SI derived unit.
The dekatherm is a unit of energy used to measure natural gas. One dekatherm is equal to 10 therms or one million British thermal units (Btu).

Megawatt-Day is used to measure energy generated in one day by a power-plant. Is commonly used to define fuel-burnup. A commonly used measure of fuel burnup is the fission energy release per unit mass of fuel.

In electric power transmission and distribution, Million volt-ampere reactive (Mvar) is a unit by which reactive power is expressed in an AC electric power system. Reactive power is the power that is wasted and not used to do work on the load.

A megavolt-ampere (MVA) is the unit used for the apparent power in an electrical circuit, equal to the product of root-mean-square (RMS) voltage and RMS current. In direct current (DC) circuits, this product is equal to the real power (active power) in watts. Volt-amperes are useful only in the context of alternating current (AC) circuits.

Start time is cCommon in IoT, databases, and time series analysis.  End time is common in finance time series analysis.

Used to identify if the time series is recording raw data or aggregated data. Possible values are Raw or Aggregated. Raw data is collected at the defined interval as a single measurement. This data is usually highly voluminous. Aggregated time series data is used with continuous or high-frequency data (say, every second), but only stores one value per interval (like an hour), the value used within that period must be an aggregation such  as: Max - the highest observed value in the hour (e.g., max temperature). Min - the lowest observed value in the hour (e.g., min heart rate). First - the earliest value recorded in that hour (open price in finance). Last - the latest value recorded in that hour (close price in finance). Mean / Sum, Median, and  Percentile are other forms of possible aggregation. The aggregation performed should be associated with the concept recording the measurement as an aggregation property.

This data type is required to represent dates at varying levels of temporal precision, from year only through to full date-time. This is needed for financial reporting scenarios where the exact date of a transaction or contract event is not known with full precision — for example, an investment schedule where the maturity year and month of a bond are known but not the exact day. Fabricating a full date in such cases would misrepresent the precision of the data. The type accepts values conforming to ISO 8601 truncated date representations: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.
